summary: Polygon's guide helps players choose a class in Baldur's Gate 3, which has 12 classes and 46 subclasses. It argues that all classes are fairly balanced and that the choice comes down to playstyle, then ranks each class by difficulty and gives a best-for category and a recommended subclass for each. It also covers the out-of-combat effects of Ability Scores and the tradeoff between Origin and custom characters.
one_line: Polygon's guide to picking a Baldur's Gate 3 class, covering all 12 classes, their strengths, and a recommended subclass for each.
key_facts: Baldur's Gate 3 has 12 classes and 46 subclasses in total.
The guide says no class is the single best (barrelmancer aside), because the classes are fairly well-balanced and the choice depends on how you want to play.

Each class's primary Ability Score is the character's highest score, which also affects out-of-combat skills; Bards and Sorcerers are Charisma-based and good at Persuasion, Deception, and Intimidation.
Origin characters let you play a party NPC from the start but limit you to that character's predetermined story, while custom characters give more freedom to experience the whole story.
The guide ranks classes subjectively by difficulty, placing casters toward the harder end because of spells and spell slots.
Fighter is the best melee class for beginners and gets subclasses Battle Master, Eldritch Knight, and Champion at level 3; Champion is recommended.
Ranger is the best ranged class for beginners, uses Dexterity, and picks a Favored Enemy at level 1; Hunter is the recommended subclass.
Barbarian is the best class for damage thanks to Rage; Berserker is the recommended subclass over Wildheart and Wild Magic.
Druid is the best class for magic and can shapeshift into a badger, wolf, spider, or cat; Circle of the Moon is recommended and adds a bear form.
Rogue is the best stealth class and can use Dash, Disengage, and Hide as Bonus Actions; Thief is the recommended subclass.
Paladin is the best class for melee and magic, with Oath of the Ancients recommended; Monk is the best for speed, with Way of the Open Palm recommended.
Warlock is the best magic class for beginners, Cleric is the best healer (Light Domain recommended, from seven Domains), and Bard is the best support class (College of Valor recommended).
Wizard is the only Intelligence-based class and has the most spells and spell slots, with eight schools of magic; Evocation is recommended.
Sorcerer is the best class for social interactions and picks its subclass at character creation; Draconic Bloodline is recommended.
The article names Great Old One as the best Warlock subclass but mislabels it as a Sorcerer subclass and points to the Sorcerer build guide.
